title: Custom Serial Dilution for Protein Quantification
author: Opentrons

steps.title: Load CSV and set labware parameters
steps.instruction: Load the input CSV file that assigns each of the 48 protein samples (samples 1‑48, column‑wise across two 24‑tube racks) to one of the six dilution schemes; in the protocol UI specify the labware type for the diluent reservoir and enter the required dead‑volume amount for that reservoir.

steps.title: Check diluent volume
steps.instruction: When the protocol pauses, verify that the reservoir contains sufficient diluent volume for the selected scheme (accounting for dead volume) before proceeding.

steps.title: Pick up P300 tips for current samples
steps.instruction: For each dilution scheme, the P300 multi‑channel pipette will pick up a number of tips equal to the number of samples being processed in that block (maximum 8 tips).

steps.title: Dispense diluent into destination columns
steps.instruction: Using the P300 multi‑channel, transfer the appropriate diluent volume from the reservoir into the destination columns on the dilution plate for the current samples; the number of columns filled is two to four depending on the dilution scheme.

steps.title: Add samples with P20
steps.instruction: Using the single‑channel P20 pipette, transfer each current protein sample into the corresponding well of the first destination column that was just filled with diluent.

steps.title: Perform serial dilution
steps.instruction: With the P300 multi‑channel, execute the serial‑dilution sequence defined for the scheme: mix the sample in the first column the specified number of repeats, then transfer the mixture to the next column, repeating until all dilution points are completed.

steps.title: Generate output file
steps.instruction: After all dilution schemes have been processed, the protocol creates a downloadable output file that lists the dilution‑plate destination well for each input sample.

steps.title: Download output file via Opentrons app
steps.instruction: In the Opentrons app, go to Devices → your robot → three‑dot menu → Robot Settings → Advanced → Launch Jupyter Notebook; from the notebook interface locate and download the generated output file to your computer.
